title: A Current for the Escarpment
premise: Freya Dunmore, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate, drags her salvaged research rig through river country chasing weather that pays. When spring floods surrender a chest bearing the seal of Karstia—a nation erased from every map—Freya and her reluctant partner Tomas realize the chest's contents name them as heirs to something the Syndicate has hunted for decades. Pursued by debt collectors who double as assassins, they race across the Escarpment before early snows seal the passes, guided by fragments of a dead woman's memory encoded in the chest itself. At the summit, Freya must choose between selling the inheritance to buy her freedom and claiming it, knowing that claiming it means becoming visible—and accountable—for the first time in years.
about_author: Casper Joubert is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent a decade mapping floodplains across three continents before turning to fiction. They write from a converted grain silo and remain, by preference, difficult to find.

chapters.title: The Debt of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Chasing a supercell across flatland for a syndicate client, she calculates storm data against what she owes the Vane Syndicate. A near-miss lightning strike destroys half her sensor array. Beat: competence masking desperation; we learn she never stays anywhere longer than a season.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. After the flood crests, Tomas—Freya's navigator and conscience—spots the chest snagged in willow roots. He pulls it out against Freya's instinct to leave strange things alone. Beat: curiosity winning over caution, the first crack in their survival routine.

chapters.title: A Seal No One Should Recognize
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The chest bears the Karstian double-eagle, a nation scrubbed from atlases after the Annexation. Inside: a brass orrery, a ledger of names, and a letter addressed to 'the Dunmore line.' Beat: dread—the past has found her by name.

chapters.title: The Optimists Call
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Vane Syndicate enforcer Ilse Rook arrives with a smile and an offer: hand over the chest, and the debt dissolves. Freya stalls. That night their camp is searched. Beat: the trap closing; staying invisible was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Studying the ledger, Freya finds her grandmother's name among Karstian custodians—and learns the orrery is a key to a vault beneath the Escarpment holding the nation's confiscated archive. Beat: inheritance reframed as burden, not treasure.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They break camp at 3 a.m., rigging the truck to read as abandoned. Rook's second team picks up their trail within hours. A river ford nearly drowns the orrery. Beat: flight begins; trust between Freya and Tomas tested under pressure.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They shelter in Halvett, a border town built on Karstian ruins where locals deny the old names. An archivist's granddaughter, Mirela, recognizes the seal and offers help—at a price. Beat: memory as contraband; some communities chose forgetting to survive.

chapters.title: Rook's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilse Rook's POV. Rook calculates the Syndicate's interest in the vault: not gold but leverage—the archive proves the Annexation was engineered. She reports to her superior, who orders no witnesses. Beat: antagonist humanized but committed; the stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: Mirela's Map
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Mirela trades them her grandfather's smuggled route over the Escarpment for a promise: bring back one document proving Karstia existed. Freya refuses to promise anything. Beat: friction over whether survival justifies abandoning others' hopes.

chapters.title: First Snowline
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The high passes show early snow, weeks ahead of season. Weather models say they have six days. Rook's team burns a bridge behind them, cutting retreat. Beat: point of no return; the mountain becomes both enemy and ally.

chapters.title: The Orrery Speaks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. At altitude, the orrery responds to geomagnetic readings—Freya realizes it's also a survey instrument, and its needle points not to the summit vault but off-route toward a dead station. Beat: revelation that the chest wants to be found; wonder amid exhaustion.

chapters.title: Station Kestrel
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The derelict weather station holds a Karstian scientist's final logs—she stayed through the Annexation recording data no one would ever read. Freya sees her own future in it. Beat: mirror moment; the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Col
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Rook's team corners them at a mountain col. In the fight, the orrery is seized—but Tomas hides the ledger, and Mirela's route knowledge lets them escape down a glacier chute. Beat: costly victory; Freya injured, morale fracturing.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A storm pins them for two days in a snow cave with dwindling fuel. Delirious, Freya confesses why she keeps moving: her family's Karstian ties got her parents killed, and invisibility felt like penance. Beat: emotional nadir and intimacy; grief finally spoken.

chapters.title: What Tomas Carried
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas reveals he's known about the chest since the river—he'd read the letter first and said nothing, hoping to protect her from choosing. Freya's fury gives way to understanding. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness; partnership rebuilt on honesty rather than habit.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's True Client
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Intercepted orders reveal the Syndicate answers to descendants of the Annexation's architects, who need the archive destroyed before a restitution tribunal convenes in spring. Rook hesitates for the first time. Beat: antagonist's crisis of loyalty; moral fault lines widen.

chapters.title: The Last Ascent
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Final climb through wind shear, using storm-reading skills honed over years of running to navigate instead of flee. Tomas anchors the rope; Mirela's map ends here. Beat: all threads converging; fear transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Ice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The orrery, recovered from Rook's fallen lieutenant, opens a fissure-sheltered chamber: thousands of documents, photographs, recordings—the proof a nation lived. Beat: awe and vertigo; inheritance fully revealed as collective, not personal.

chapters.title: Rook at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Rook arrives alone, weapon drawn, orders ambiguous. Freya offers her the choice her employers denied her: witness or executioner. Sirens of an approaching avalanche force the decision. Beat: climax; Rook lowers the gun and helps seal the chamber's entrance against the Syndicate.

chapters.title: Burial by Snow
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The avalanche entombs the pass—and with it, temporarily, the vault, safe from retrieval until spring. Rook, now a defector, carries testimony that could convict her employers. Beat: survival redefined; the mountain that threatened them becomes the guardian.

chapters.title: Spring Tribunal
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Months later, in a courtroom in the lowlands, the first documents surface publicly. Freya testifies under her real family name—Dunmore-Karsti—for the first time. The debt is voided; the visibility she feared becomes standing. Beat: resolution; memory honored, inheritance claimed.

chapters.title: A Current for the Escarpment
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, coda. She and Tomas return to Halvett with Mirela's promised document, then drive toward the next storm season—not fleeing now, but choosing. The last line mirrors the first: stopping costs less than it used to. Beat: quiet hope; movement transformed from escape into direction.
